programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.desc: Madeira - Portugal's autonomous island in the Atlantic Ocean, is closer to the African coast than to the mother country Portugal, from which it is separated by about 900 kilometers. The island's name comes from Portuguese sailors who claimed the uninhabited isle for themselves in 1419. Madeira means wood and that was available in abundance. Almost the entire surface was covered by dense forest. Since 1982, two-thirds of the landscape has been protected.

programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.desc: The "Parque Natural da Ria Formosa" is one of the largest lagoon conservation areas in Europe. Bordered by five natural islands. A mosaic of sandbanks, brackish and freshwater lagoons and salt marshes. In 2010, the "Ria Formosa" was chosen as one of the seven natural wonders of Portugal. It is a unique ecosystem: in the winter months, more than 20,000 birds gather here. In addition, the nature park has one of the largest seahorse populations internationally. More than half of all fish species in the Atlantic are said to spawn in the lagoon.

programme.title: Northern Woods
programme.desc: It is a musical film a a tributeto the Nordic forest: it shows its development from a primeval wood to a cultivated forest. Once populated by wild animals such as wolves, bears, eagles, deer and musk oxen, complex re-enactment-scenes shot by dollies and helicopters vividly depict the colonization of the forest by the Celts and Germans. But as time progressed, the northern forest has on numerous occasions fallen victim to environmental degradation and overexploitation. Several provisions were made to protect this wild beauty. The Helsinki resolution of 1993, which stipulated that the woods be used in a way and in a magnitude which guarantees their biological variety and productiveness and vitality, is but one measure put in place to secure the preservation of the natural gem. Time-lapse photography and breath-taking shots show our main protagonist – the woods – in its stunning glory. This beautiful wooded land, changes throughout the seasons. Our woodland is a world-renowned ecological jewel. It is famous, well-known and loved by tourists, forest economists, environmentalists, historians and intellectuals alike.

programme.title: Germany's Mystic Forest
programme.desc: 2.000 rivers and streams dig deep into the underground and transport their water into reservoirs or "Germany's Wild Amazon", the Wupper. These forests and rivers, together with heathlands and moors, are home to a diverse fauna. Martens, badgers, wild boars, hares, roe deer, and red deer, even black grouse and hazel deer find shelter in these parts. Wolves also have a dominant presence, not to mention those who live underground, such as lizards, bats, and snakes. Accompany us on a journey where we explore every corner of this rugged land. Climb underground into the Bergisches Land, through the vast hidden cave systems that sprawl far beneath the forests. There is also much to be discovered in the water, dive with us in crystal clear streams and rivers with their diverse flora and fauna.

programme.title: Chiemgau, A Changing Landscape
programme.desc: A few thousand years ago, there were bare moraine ridges and barren meltwater valleys here. A landscape born in the last ice age, characterized by the edge of the Alps, gentle hills, moors, and lakes. And by cultural richness, not only on the islands in Lake Chiemsee, with their famous monasteries and castles. Long before King Ludwig II, the first people settled in the Chiemgau region. Finds of hunting weapons from the Neanderthal era prove that the land was inhabited even during the ice age, probably because there was plenty of game to hunt. During the Bronze Age, one of the most important trade routes from the mountains to the Alpine foothills passed through here. Then came the Celts and the Romans.

programme.title: Chiemgau, A Changing Landscape
programme.desc: Three times in the past two decades, the Chiemsee area has experienced "once-in-a-century" floods. Climate, wildlife, and landscape have changed, and it seems this transformation is accelerating. Species living in the flood zones are developing sophisticated survival strategies. Knot ants, for instance, place their queen in the middle and form a raft with their bodies, even conquering new habitats. Flooding is less of a disaster for nature and impacts humans more significantly.

programme.title: Bavarian Forest - Deep, Dark and Enchanted
programme.desc: After an unusual mass reproduction of bark beetles in the nineties, thousands hectares of old spruce forest were destroyed. Soon after, a new, healthier forest started to grow – a new primeval forest. Within a few years, in place of the former monoculture, a diverse forest developed, rich in spruces, ashes, beech and fir trees. Naturally, this diversity has in turn attracted new animal and plant species. Even lynx and otters returned and made Bavaria their home again.

programme.title: mareTV: Sweden's High Coast
programme.desc: Sweden's Höga Kusten (High Coast) has been rising by almost one centimetre per year since the last ice age 10,000 years ago. This has created a hilly Baltic Sea landscape on the Gulf of Bothnia with small and large islands. Untouched nature, dense forests and energetic, rather idiosyncratic islanders have plenty of room there. Every year at the end of August a biting stench mixes with the fresh Baltic Sea breeze. For weeks the so-called sour herring, Swedish: Surströmming, is fermented in brine. Ruben Madsen is a producer of surströmming and an absolute connoisseur. In his wooden hut on the island of Ulvön he puts the herring in according to a traditional recipe. At the start of the season, the cans are opened for the first time. Lovers of the "stinky fish" then come from all over the world to taste the now world-famous delicacy in cans. Opening the cans of "rotten fish" is considered internationally as a test of courage, people film themselves doing so, the inhabitants of the High Coast can only smile about it.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: It is one of the wildest roads in Asia: the Trans Sulawesi Highway. The adventurous road leads through Indonesia's fourth-largest island and takes people to spectacular destinations. To beautiful beaches, turbulent cities, or unique primeval forests.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: In the extreme north-east of Norway known as the Finnmark region, winters are freezing cold and snowy. Due to the location on the Arctic Ocean, the roads are prone to snow drifts. Every metre is a challenge and a journey into risk. An adventure for all those who set off into the fascinating and unique landscape, through a seemingly endless desert of snow.

programme.title: mareTV: Corsica - Fascinating Mountain World in the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Corsica looks like an alpine landscape in the Mediterranean, an island with dramatic rock formations, romantic bays and proud inhabitants who see themselves first and foremost as Corsicans and only then as French. The Greeks in ancient times called the island Kalliste: the beautiful. We explore this fascinating mountain world in the Mediterranean.

programme.title: Baltic National Parks
programme.desc: Soomaa National Park is one of Europes wettest wilderness areas. Floods, forests and wetlands create a landscape where canoes replace roads during the fifth season.

programme.title: Baltic National Parks
programme.desc: Gauja National Park in Latvia features diverse wildlife, red sandstone cliffs and a winding river that flows through forests shaped by long human history.

programme.title: The Secret world of Herbs
programme.desc: Secluded for many centuries in inaccessible valleys, the inhabitants of the Alps had no alternative but to rely on the healing powers of nature. A knowledge of herbs was deeply rooted in these mountain-dwellers’ everyday lives – until the twentieth century, when this wisdom became eclipsed by modern academic medicine. Today, Alpine herbs are witnessing a revival, as public interest in regional natural treasures grows. The potential of Alpine herbs is far from exhausted. In the Berchtesgaden Alps, the film shows Hubsi Ilsanker at work as a root-digger, a back-breaking job that has scarcely changed in four hundred years. Authorized by a special historic permit to supply the oldest gentian distillery in Germany, Hubsi digs for protected gentian roots in Berchtesgaden National Park. For yellow gentian is one of the most bitter medicinal herbs in the world, well suited for schnapps and as a general tonic.

programme.title: The Secret world of Herbs
programme.desc: In the pristine nature and mild climate of southeastern Europe grows a unique diversity of wild plants. Far removed from major industry and polluted soils, the Balkan countries have become the largest exporter of herbs in Europe. In Bulgaria alone, more than 300,000 people work with domestic plants. The business is becoming increasingly lucrative. The film takes us to the Croatian coast. On the Adriatic island of Cres, the audience meets Mladen Dragoslavić. In May, when the sage begins to blossom, this beekeeper has one month to produce his income for an entire year – always with the goal of creating the best sage honey in the Balkans. Given a choice, the bees would never choose sage, for entering and exiting the narrow blossom is strenuous. Within three weeks, maximum, Mladen must remove his bees from the island. Otherwise they will die of exhaustion. In Skopje, the capital of Macedonia, the film visits Iva Yosifova. Hollyhock provides the raw material for her objects of art. The herb is medically beneficial, due to its mucilage, which is added to many cough tea mixtures. Iva, though, makes paper from hollyhock. Thanks to the herb’s long fibres, the paper can be spread onto objects and modeled. The technique produces delicate sculptures, as fragile as nature.

programme.title: Stories of the Mediterranean Forest: Sierra Morena
programme.desc: The Mediterranean Basin is one of the planet’s most biologically rich and complex regions. The crossroads of Europe, Asia and Africa is considered to be one of Earth’s biodiversity hotspots. A vast number of both animal and plant species unique to the region live in its various habitats. The Mediterranean Basin is located in one of the planet’s temperate zones. The subtropical climate makes it colder and wet here in winter, hot and dry in summer and mild and rainy in autumn and spring.

programme.title: Fertile Floods - Croatia's Wetlands
programme.desc: Every year, in the middle of Croatia, it's the same story: after the annual snowmelt, a huge flood wave spills out of the Alps toward Zagreb and Belgrade. This leads to an increase in the River Sava's water levels of some ten metres. The contents of more than ten billion bathtubs floods an area the size of Lake Constance, often for months on end, yet still the Croatian and Serbian capital is spared a flood disaster. One of the reasons for this is the fact that the Sava is able to flow unhindered. The annual floods not only create a natural retention reservoir for flood control: alongside the Sava lies a natural paradise, unique in Central Europe. In the species-rich, alluvial flood forests of the last major meadow landscapes of the continent, enormous predatory fish like the catfish lie in wait for prey. The fertile floodplains of the Sava are an important resting place for more than 240 bird species, including Hoopoe, great crested Grebe, little Egret, common snipe and pied Avocet. Old, domestic livestock breeds like the Turopolje pig and Posavina horse spend almost the entire year in the floodplains. They appreciate the alluvial meadows, keep puddles and mudholes open whilst wallowing and, as living lawnmowers, they ensure that the moist meadows aren't transformed into dense oak forests. Thanks to this traditional pasture farming, more than 700 pairs of white stork alone breed in the Lonjsko Polje National Park. The Sava Floodplains allow us to glance into the past of our continent and at the same time, illustrate just how flood protection for major towns can be perfected.

programme.title: Europe's Wild River - The Elbe - 1.000 Miles of Wildlife and Nature
programme.desc: The river rises in the Czech Giant Mountains. Here it is called the Labe. After Děčín it flows into Germany and is called Elbe. There are various explanations for the origin of the river name "Elbe". One often mentioned is the Latin name of the river "albia", which means "bright water". This would also explain why the stream is referred to with the feminine article "the Elbe", since the Latin term "albia" is also feminine. Rather poetic than linguistically probable, however, is the explanation that elves (Middle High German: alb) scurrying around the pines in the white river mists could have helped the river to get its name. Geographically, the river can be divided into different sections: The Upper Elbe is the part from the source to about Riesa in the administrative district of Dresden, which is more characterized by mountains. The Middle Elbe, on the other hand, is a lowland river. It reaches as far as the Geesthacht dam just outside Hamburg. The Lower Elbe is called the tidal part of the river. Here, the Elbe forms an estuary, a so-called estuary. At high tide, seawater enters this funnel-shaped delta at the mouth of the Elbe and mixes with the freshwater of the river. At low tide, the water then flows off to the North Sea. Finally, the continuation of the estuary funnel in the Wadden Sea is called the Outer Elbe.

programme.title: Masai Mara: The Big Hunt
programme.desc: When food supply in the Serengeti dwindles, the Masai Mara is a paradise for predators. As the black wildebeests, gazelles, zebras and antelopes make their yearly trip from the south of the Serengeti to the north, nature’s best laid trap, the Mara River in Kenya is waiting ahead. Captivating shots filmed under water show how crocodiles prepare for the Big Hunt while other predators lurk on the banks awaiting their bounty. The biggest problems for the migratory animals are the Mara and the Tarek River, where they have to put their lives at risk to get to the other side. A great number of them die as they jump into the river and break their legs, while others are carried away by the drift or drown. Those who are not victims of the river itself risk falling prey to the crocodiles. We entered this unchartered territory, the crocodile domain by heading under water. Follow these predators in and around their habitat and watch prides of lions map out their game plan. In slow-motion, we show you the final showdown between predator and prey. Will it be a successful hunt or will the hoofed animals persevere?

programme.title: Magical Moors
programme.desc: Wide open heaths, windswept and barren in winter, are transformed into wonderful carpets of white, fluffy cotton grass in summer. Large bears and wolves roam alongside delicately fluttering butterflies, the bubbling calls of black grouse and the enchanting trills of the great snipe. Moors, bogs and wetlands can be found all over in Europe. Everyone has at least heard about this habitat but most know little about it. It is an ancient yet largely unknown set of landscapes that is full of enchanting surprises. On a warm spring day, poisonous adders emerge from hiding to perform their impressive mating dance. As dusk falls, snipe gather on traditional leks, leaping and singing to impress the opposite sex. And deep down in the boggy marshes, glittering emeralds of sticky dew lure insects into the deadly arms of meat-eating plants. Magical Moors captures the quiet beauty of a spectacular landscape, and its often elusive wildlife, in stunning detail.

programme.title: Aurora - Fire in the Sky
programme.desc: In the earth’s polar regions, a ghostly flicker and colourful glow often brighten the night sky. Whoever sees an aurora event will never forget this impressive experience. Finland’s Saami people, Alaska’s Inuit, Canada’s Native Americans and New Zealand’s Maori all have legends about the origins and meaning of this magic natural spectacle. These stories tell of spirits dancing in the sky, of a bright and better world where hunting game is abundant, of battling gods and celestial messages.

programme.title: 15th Meridian East - Similarity in Difference
programme.desc: The journey leads from the Norwegian Vesterålen to Chad, the Aeolian Islands and the Polish Giant Mountains. As different as the landscapes and cultures may be, all people are united in their love for their children and their desire to give something to tomorrow's generation.

programme.title: 15th Meridian East - Similarity in Difference
programme.desc: What ideas are people on the 15th meridian east developing to shape the future and leave tomorrow's generations a home worth living in? This consequence leads us to four future designers. From the barren Namib Desert to the glacier worlds of Spitsbergen, Sicily and the Croatian Mediterranean.

programme.title: Gronland - In the Glare of Ice
programme.desc: Greenland is the largest island in the world and the landmass closest to the North Pole. 80% of the country is covered by a layer of ice up to 3000 meters thick. Most of the inhabitants of the country are spread over the breathtaking landscape of the ice-free west coast. The country is mostly inhabited by Inuit, who have been feeding on what nature has provided them for thousands of years. But the original life is in a state of change. The modernisation of society and man-made global warming threaten the Arctic natural paradise that is so incredibly important for our planet. Through the eyes of locals we get to know the authentic Greenland.

programme.title: Dust And Stripes
programme.desc: In a never-ending quest for grass and water, the striped herds undertake an annual epic trek across the vast lunar landscape of the Kalahari’s Makgadikgadi Pans. Most of the year, the Makgadikgadi is an inhospitable wasteland of windswept, salt-encrusted pans. For the area’s water-dependent zebra, the Boteti River on the western edge of the pans is a dry-season lifeline. However, it is also a death trap, with lions waiting in ambush and crocodiles lurking in dark riverside caves.

programme.title: Alpine Lakes - Dark Depths and Icy Heights
programme.desc: This is a nature documentary, which leads us into the fascinating world of deep mountain lakes. We conquer ice palaces of unsuspected beauty. In the freezers, in which elves, fairies and mountain trolls once did their mischief, we move, using a special breathing technique and with special cameras in search of nocturnal hunters, whose eyes are equipped with residual light amplifying receptors.

programme.title: Maury

programme.title: Steve Wilkos
programme.desc: Deshawn afirma que su ex Lynette abandonó a su hijo de 5 años. Pero ella afirma que él la está alejando de su hijo. Sin embargo, Deshawn se enteró recientemente de que no está en el certificado de nacimiento de su hijo, ¡así que quiere una prueba de ADN!

programme.title: Steve Wilkos
programme.desc: El 27 de abril de 2011, un tornado azotó Tuscaloosa, Alabama, causando daños masivos y víctimas. La hija de Toye, Latoya, fue reportada como desaparecida, pero la policía la investigó como homicidio. ¿Tuvo Toye algo que ver con su desaparición?

programme.title: Jerry Springer
programme.desc: La novia de Nick descubre por qué él pasa tanto tiempo con su vecina; el novio de Osha tiene una aventura con su amiga; Brandi resiente el comportamiento imprudente de su novio después de todos los sacrificios que ha hecho para mantener su relación.

programme.title: Jerry Springer
programme.desc: La nueva novia de Barin tiene un secreto; Ericka desaprueba a la novia de su hermana; otro hombre puede arruinar la boda de Tyler.

programme.desc: Carl ha venido a decirle a su novia que se ha estado acostando con su peor enemiga, Keisha. A continuación, Donte le dirá a su mejor amigo, Quincy, que está acostándose con su prometida. Después, Janel y Nikkie están peleando por el mismo hombre.

programme.title: Jerry Springer
programme.desc: Una mujer encuentra un romance con la hermana gemela de su prometido; un hombre recurre a otra mujer en busca de atención; un hombre le dice a la madre de su hijo que quiere estar con otra persona.

programme.title: Jerry Springer
programme.desc: El marido de Darleen dice que es adicto a los clubes de striptease; el novio de Mary está obsesionado con limpiar su coche, y ella sospecha que lo está usando como tapadera para algo más; el miedo de Jesse al compromiso lo mete en problemas.

programme.title: Séptimo Día
programme.desc: Jhon Ferney, condenado por feminicidio en 2015, muestra los efectos de la celopatía, trastorno originado en la infancia por la falta de afecto. Su historia revela cómo los celos enfermizos y una relación tóxica desembocaron en tragedia.

programme.title: Séptimo Día
programme.desc: Un productor de Séptimo Día graba cómo en un bar en Bucaramanga se alquilan niños para mendicidad. Yiriam y Franklin, migrantes venezolanos, pierden a su hija menor tras dejarla al cuidado de Franyeli, quien es detenida por mendicidad ajena. La Policía y el ICBF intervienen en varios casos similares.

programme.title: Séptimo Día
programme.desc: Un hombre respetado por la sociedad y admirado como cristiano ejemplar oculta su rostro de agresor dentro de su hogar. Cuando su esposa desaparece, su familia inicia una lucha desesperada por descubrir la verdad detrás de su fachada intachable.

programme.title: Séptimo Día
programme.desc: Los ataques de perros peligrosos a niños aumentan en Colombia. Aunque existen leyes, muchos dueños siguen sin responsabilizarse. Las víctimas enfrentan lesiones graves, y las autoridades luchan contra la impunidad, mientras los ataques continúan.

programme.title: Séptimo Día
programme.desc: Jhon Fredy y Miguel Ángel adoptaron una niña, pero el Colegio Americano de Bogotá los rechazó por ser una familia homoparental. Fabio Meneses y Xiomy Díaz sufrieron en terapias de conversión. Andrés Felipe Arboleda fue asesinado por discriminación en Caldas.

programme.title: Séptimo Día
programme.desc: Estafas de vehículos usados en Colombia afectan a numerosos compradores. Desde autos embargados hasta ventas de vehículos robados, los casos incluyen varios imputados, como Norman Eduardo Serrano y Óscar Fabián Rodríguez.

programme.title: Séptimo Día
programme.desc: El miedo a las represalias ha impedido que las víctimas denuncien delitos en Colombia.

programme.title: El Rastro
programme.desc: En 2016, en Socorro, Santander, Yesenia Bernal fue asesinada para robarle a su bebé recién nacido. Su amiga Edilsa María Díaz, tras perder su propio embarazo y temiendo perder a su pareja, fingió estar embarazada y planeó el crimen junto a Juan Carlos Vega para apropiarse de la niña. Ambos fueron capturados y condenados: Edilsa a 35 años y Juan Carlos a una pena similar.

programme.title: El Rastro
programme.desc: En 2009, Islanis fue asesinada a los 21 años. El principal sospechoso, alias "Betún", reveló que el verdadero autor intelectual era Jonatán Pérez, un cabo del Ejército, quien la mató al enterarse de su embarazo, temiendo el impacto en su carrera militar. En 2011, Pérez fue condenado a 40 años de prisión por homicidio agravado.

programme.title: El Rastro
programme.desc: EL caso de un asesinato planeado por una pareja, para quitar del medio a un humilde carpintero con el objetivo quedarse con su fortuna. Hoy los hijos, del ahora difunto, exigen justicia para que los verdaderos culpables paguen las consecuencias de sus actos.

programme.title: El Rastro
programme.desc: En Cajamarca, Tolima, el líder ambientalista César García fue asesinado frente a su familia tras oponerse a la minera AngloGold Ashanti. Aunque se sospechó de un vínculo con la empresa, las autoridades lo descartaron. Una carta de suicidio reveló que el verdadero autor fue Álvaro Meléndez, vecino con quien García tuvo un litigio de tierras. Meléndez permanece detenido esperando juicio.

programme.title: El Rastro
programme.desc: Gina Paola Manrique, empresaria de Neiva, fue hallada muerta en un aparente suicidio. Tras investigar, el CTI determinó que fue feminicidio.

programme.title: El Rastro
programme.desc: Melany Amaya, de 16 años, desapareció tras asistir a una fiesta electrónica en Medellín en junio de 2018. Tras siete días de búsqueda, una llamada anónima alertó a su madre. Su cuerpo fue hallado en un potrero del sector "El Calvario".

programme.title: Juez Mom
programme.desc: Mario está demandando a la psíquica del vecindario, Lydia, por $30,000 y la imposición negligente de angustia emocional después de prometer eliminar su maldición ... por una tarifa.

programme.title: Juez Mom
programme.desc: Giselle está demandando a su padre, Albert Martinez, por angustia emocional y $145,000 por el costo de cancelar su boda.

programme.title: Juez Mom
programme.desc: Miguel está demandando a su ex novia, Jasmine, por la totalidad de los $5 millones que ella ganó a través de un boleto instantáneo que compró con su tarjeta de crédito.

programme.title: Juez Mom
programme.desc: Guadalupe está demandando a Thomas, el dueño de una tienda de vestidos de Quinceañera, por dolor y sufrimiento más el costo del vestido que es de $4,500.

programme.title: Los Informantes
programme.desc: A los 16 años, Liliana Cáceres se hizo famosa en Barranquilla al fingir un embarazo de nueve bebés, tras enterarse de la infidelidad de su novio con su mejor amiga. Su mentira, que incluso llegó a oídos de Gabriel García Márquez, se descubrió al someterse a exámenes médicos. Tras el escándalo, huyó a Cartagena, rehízo su vida y hoy sueña con ayudar a niñas embarazadas de verdad.

programme.title: Los Informantes
programme.desc: Cinco años después del homicidio de Alonso Orjuela, dueño de Surtifruver, su exesposa Cecilia Rueda y su socio Mauricio Parra hablan por primera vez ante cámaras. Ambos estuvieron presos —ella acusada de complicidad, él de ser testaferro de las FARC— pero fueron liberados por vencimiento de términos. Ahora denuncian un montaje judicial y afirman tener pruebas de que no fue un crimen pasional.

programme.desc: Diamond asegura que SP le rogó un hijo, Jenell dice que él quería otro con ella, pero SP lo niega todo. ¿Debe Tone $3,000 en manutención? ¿Es Jacob el padre del hijo de Tyler y Matina? ¡Hoy en MAURY!

programme.title: Maury
programme.desc: ¡Cartel se niega a creer que una aventura de una noche con una amiga de la escuela secundaria, Brittany, resultó en su embarazo! Entonces, ¿Juan y Clinton son los papás de sus hijos? Además, ¡Kelly necesita saber qué primo fue el padre de su bebé!

programme.title: Local Knowledge
programme.desc: The next stop on our Florida Keys adventure brings Rush Maltz to the legendary waters of Islamorada — a destination known for its laid-back island vibe, world-class fishing, fine dining, and easy access to the reef. Joining locals Jimmy Hendrix and Jordi Hortensi, the game plan is simple: check in by boat, chase fish, eat well, and go dive. From kite fishing the reef to fresh seafood and great company, this episode is all about experiencing the true rhythm of a Florida Keys vacation.

programme.title: Road Trip Angler
programme.desc: In this episode of Road Trip Angler, host Jameson Redding takes guests Jesse Laspeyre and Brooks Beatty on a multi-day adventure exploring the Forgotten Coast along the Florida Adventure Trail, chasing fish and adventure at every turn.

programme.title: Destination Dive
programme.desc: Experience the magic of shore diving from one of the Keys’ most scenic beaches. The episode also follows military veterans discovering healing and renewed purpose through diving.

programme.title: Dirt
programme.desc: New. York. City. That’s where our host Josh Rosen kicks off his journey in Episode 4—and where he lived for 16 years and started up the surf-centric apparel brand, Saturdays NYC. Back in his old stomping grounds, Josh first meets up with the award-winning chef and Mumbai native, Chintan Pandya, currently blowing up the New York food scene with his unapologetic and authentic Indian cuisine (pro tip: try the goat brains). Next, Josh travels through the boroughs, heads upstate, and along the coast to source local ingredients—from sake brewers and pig farmers to catching fresh lobster just 100 miles from Wall Street. As always the adventure will end with a feast, right back in Chintan’s kitchen.

programme.title: Hard Truths of Conservation
programme.desc: In the heart of the Zambezi Delta, a team of conservationists have overseen one of the largest range expansions of African lions in modern times. From a reintroduction of 24 lions in 2018, today the population is more than a hundred.

programme.title: The Green Way Outdoors
programme.desc: Kyle and Jeff wade into the flooded timber of the legendary Coca-Cola Woods, where mallards drop through the treetops in waves. Amidst echoes of calling and wingbeats, they experience one of America’s most iconic duck hunts.

programme.title: Destination Dive
programme.desc: In this episode, we will highlight what’s being done in the Florida Keys to protect and save the reefs. We will show innovative solutions researchers have created to protect the coral and showcase the recovery that’s taking place.

programme.title: Stomping Grounds
programme.desc: From battling towering 12-foot waves in the Gulf of Alaska, to reeling in colossal 200 lb. halibut, they discover firsthand the rugged beauty of America's 49th state. This episode highlights Lindell Yachts as a top builder of rugged offshore sportfishing yachts, as well as Radon Boats as great pilothouse fishing and guide boats.

programme.title: Fox Hollow Outdoors
programme.desc: Michael continues the family tradition of fish stew and gathering, with hopes that Larkin will pass on the same traditions.

programme.title: Goin' Coastal
programme.desc: As the pressure of opening his new store builds, Josh steps away from the chaos and returns to the water for a solo wade fishing trip — his first in years.

programme.title: Canadian Whitetail
programme.desc: With few mature bucks to hunt Dean heads out to put his time in regardless because anything, can happen.

programme.title: Winchester Life
programme.desc: Spring in Michigan means turkey season is on. In this episode of Winchester Life, the crew returns for Turkey Camp 2025, where changing weather, early mornings, and vocal birds set the tone for the week. After dialing in their setups at the range, the team heads into the field to chase gobblers across hardwoods and open farmland. From patient sits at sunrise to midday moves and carefully planned decoy strategies, each hunt brings new challenges and opportunities. Close encounters, tough conditions, and well-timed shots highlight the grind of spring turkey hunting, as the crew makes the most of every chance in the Michigan woods.

programme.title: Winchester Life
programme.desc: In this episode of Winchester Life, the crew travels to Kodiak Island, Alaska, in pursuit of blacktail deer in some of the most remote terrain they’ve faced. After a multi-day journey by air - and sea, they arrive in a landscape defined by steep mountains, thick brush, and ever-changing weather. Once on the ground, the team confirms their setups and puts Winchester’s Supreme Long Range ammunition to the test as they glass expansive hillsides, pick apart coastal terrain, and carefully plan each move. From quick opportunities along the shoreline to calculated stalks in the high country, every moment demands focus and precision. Against the backdrop of Alaska’s wild beauty, this episode highlights the challenge, the strategy, and the performance it takes to capitalize when the opportunity finally comes together.

programme.title: Winchester Life
programme.desc: The team at Winchester Ammunition has arrived in Oregon to visit the Leupold Long Range Academy. There, they’ll put Winchester’s new “Supreme Long Range” ammunition to the test, pushing its performance across demanding long-range scenarios. - - With precision, consistency, and confidence on the line, the team is eager to demonstrate exactly what “Precision Rifle Perfected” means when every shot counts.

programme.title: Winchester Life
programme.desc: Join Benny Spies of Team Winchester as he shares stories of his upbringing in South Dakota. From cherished family photos to duck seasons of the past, learn how a passion for hunting was ignited and became a way of life for Benny and his family.

programme.title: Wilderness Chronicles
programme.desc: In this episode of The Wilderness Chronicles, we uncover true accounts from around the world that feel almost impossible. A fisherman off the coast of Chile is taken by a breaching whale. A diver vanishes into darkness and finds himself trapped inside the mouth of a humpback whale. Two kayakers are lifted from the water by something massive lurking just below the surface of the ocean. - These are not legends. These are real people telling their stories. - We also revisit one of the most powerful moments in the Bible. The story of Jonah. Scripture tells us that God prepared a great fish to swallow Jonah for a divine purpose. Could something like that still happen today? What does science say about surviving inside a whale? And are these modern encounters more than just coincidence?

programme.title: Wilderness Chronicles
programme.desc: The movie Jaws was inspired by a string of shark attacks... some in FRESHWATER! In this eerie episode of Wilderness Chronicles, Kyle Green explores the shocking reality of sharks found in freshwater. From bull sharks traveling up the Mississippi River to strange reports out of the Great Lakes, we examine how far these predators can really go. You'll hear about bull sharks in Lake Nicaragua, the science behind their survival in rivers and lakes, and theories about whether they could adapt to colder waters. It's a mix of strange history, biology, and firsthand accounts that might make you think twice before jumping in.

programme.title: Wilderness Chronicles
programme.desc: Deep in the backroads of the Midwest there are stories locals rarely tell out loud. Stories of pale figures with oversized heads watching from the trees. Stories passed down in whispers and warnings. The Melon Heads legend has haunted Michigan, Ohio, and surrounding states for decades. Some say they are the result of dark experiments. Others believe they are something far older. Something that never left the woods.

programme.title: The Green Way Outdoors
programme.desc: Kyle and Jeff hear about the dangers of fishing for Bluefin Tuna in the Atlantic Ocean from locals in Gloucester, Massachusetts. Then they head 30 miles out onto the open ocean with Darrin of Reel Respect Charters in the hopes of landing their own giant.

programme.title: The Green Way Outdoors
programme.desc: Kyle and Jeff team up with their friends from Boss Shotshells in South Dakota for a high-energy upland hunt, pursuing wild pheasants with the help of skilled hunting dogs. The adventure takes a quirky turn with a visit to the iconic Corn Palace.

programme.title: The Journey Within
programme.desc: After harvesting a tough Anatolian Chamois, Mark Peterson heads south to the Taurus Mountains for his next challenge: The Bezoar Ibex. With the pre-rut in full swing, most Ibex are in small bachelor groups. It's only a matter of time before Mark spots a mature trophy—requiring skill, patience, and a solid understanding of this rugged terrain.

programme.title: The Journey Within
programme.desc: Mark Peterson returns to the stunning island of Dugi Otok in Croatia for his third time in pursuit of a Kri Kri ibex. This Mediterranean gem offers a true sportsman's paradise, home to an incredible variety of huntable species. While the island presents opportunities for Axis Deer and other game—which Mark briefly glasses during his adventure—the primary focus remains on connecting with a quality Kri Kri Ibex. Join Mark as he navigates the familiar yet ever-challenging terrain of Dugi Otok.

programme.title: The Journey Within
programme.desc: Follow along with Mark Peterson as he heads north to Nunavut within the Arctic Circle. On this trip, he has brought along his Gunwerks muzzleloader as well as his Gunwerks rifle. With two Caribou tags and a Musk Ox tag in his pocket, he’s excited to put both firearms to use. The muzzleloader is up to bat first. With the rocky, wide open tundra terrain it makes it more of a challenge to get close enough with the muzzleloader.

programme.title: The Journey Within
programme.desc: This week is all about Woody, a fearless Jack Russle who spends his free time doing everything from Black Bear hunting in Vancouver to Sheep hunting in the mountains.

programme.title: The Journey Within
programme.desc: Mark Peterson has one more tag in his pocket after harvesting both a Central Barren Ground Caribou and a Muskox with his Gunwerks muzzleloader on day one. This time, he has his Gunwerks rifle in hand. The conditions have been perfect, but there is a front pushing in with a ton of rain coming so Mark is eager to fill his final tag before the bad weather hits. Spotting a large group of Caribou with one big one mixed in early on in the day, he is hoping to have success and end his trip to Nunavut off with a bang!

programme.title: The Journey Within
programme.desc: Mark Peterson heads out on a unique hunt for the rare Anatolian Chamois, a mountain dweller found in the high elevations of northern Turkey. With a storm rolling in, Mark hopes the weather will push the Chamois down from their usual heights, giving him a rare chance to track this prey across the challenging landscape.

programme.title: Bearded Buck
programme.desc: In this episode, we're headed out to Oklahoma to follow along with the Sharp brothers as they hunt whitetails in their home state. You never know what to expect with these two but one thing you can always rely on is that they always have some big deer to go after!

programme.title: American Heroes Outdoors
programme.desc: On this episode we travel to Rock Falls Raceway in Wisconsin to highlight our nations heroes who have made drag racing and serving our country a way of life! We also honor our next Fargo Scheels Hometown hero, Elizabeth Miller.

programme.title: American Heroes Outdoors
programme.desc: On this episode, we travel north of the border for an unforgettable PART 1 Canadian fly-in fishing trip with Mandatory Fun Outdoors. We also highlight our next Scheels Hometown Hero, Jay Strande!

programme.title: Operation Healing Heroes
programme.desc: Vietnam war veteran Don Weber recounts his amazing journey through survivors guilt, PTSD and starting over.

programme.title: Operation Healing Heroes
programme.desc: U.S. Army veteran Carlos Powell tells of family sacrifice and fighting his post service “demons.”

programme.title: The WoodHaven Way
programme.desc: It's the second day of the Alabama Turkey season, and we hit the woods with Dr. Mike Chamberlain and Aaron Warbritton from The Hunting Public in search of a longbeard. Watching turkeys just being turkeys, and spending time with great friends is why turkey hunting is just different to us.

programme.title: The WoodHaven Way
programme.desc: This one is special. We took Ron aka “Don”, a WoodHaven employee who helps assemble our pot calls, out to Tennessee for a turkey hunt he’ll never forget. After 35 years of not harvesting a Turkey, Don finally gets his shot.

programme.title: The WoodHaven Way
programme.desc: Some mornings just remind you why we do this. We found ourselves in Southwest Alabama on one of the prettiest mornings a turkey hunter could ever ask for — cool air, soft light breaking through the timber, and gobbles echoing through the hardwoods. Even better, we got to share it with a great friend, and that’s what makes hunts like this truly special. This is what turkey hunting is all about — good friends, beautiful mornings, and chasing longbeards in God’s country.

programme.title: The WoodHaven Way
programme.desc: This Kentucky trip is one we’ll be talking about for a long time. Three longbeards hit the ground, but honestly, it’s the time spent in the woods with good friends that made this hunt what it was. We had birds gobbling, lots of laughs, and a memories that will last a lifetime, and that’s what makes turkey hunting so addicting. These are the kind of hunts you don’t take for granted.

programme.title: Reel Animals
programme.desc: Capt. Mike Anderson and Capt. Ryan Rickard keep track of the catch during an epic day in Steinhatchee, FL.

programme.title: Reel Animals
programme.desc: Part 2 of this friendly competition picks right back up where things left off in Steinhatchee, FL with Capt. Mike Anderson and Capt. Ryan Rickard.

programme.title: Goin' Coastal
programme.desc: Josh and George from Two Georges Marina battle the wind and tide on a tough day of fishing which leads Josh to fish another day, solely for revenge on the Sheepshead!

programme.title: Goin' Coastal
programme.desc: Join Captain Josh and Sheriff Eric Aden for a day of fishing and fun in Destin, Florida. These two friends hit the water, catching fish both offshore and inshore, and reeling in some impressive catches. With plenty of laughs, great stories, and a few surprises along the way, this episode is all about the joy of fishing and the bond between two guys who love the sea.

programme.title: Flats Class
programme.desc: Capt. CA looks back on 20 years of Flats Class TV and picks some of his favorite moments to revisit.

programme.title: Flats Class
programme.desc: CA’s skiff gets an upgrade. Now no fish is safe.

programme.title: Flats Class
programme.desc: Low country BBQ and Redfish? What more do you want?

programme.title: Flats Class
programme.desc: CA heads to the scenic Low country of South Carolina for part one of an epic two-part redfish adventure.

programme.title: Wildbound by Forloh
programme.desc: In this episode Andy and his friend Scotty take on Kodiak Island, Alaska for an adventure of Salmon fishing and hunting black tail deer. Whilst traversing steep mountains in the company of Kodiak brown bears and taking on cold Alaskan waters, Andy presents useful information for fellow outdoor enthusiasts all whilst building friendships with the great people of Kodiak Big Timber Lodge.

programme.title: Wildbound by Forloh
programme.desc: In this episode Andy goes back to his home farm in Alabama for deer and quail hunting. Not only does he make incredible dishes with his former ‘masterchef’ contestant Alex which he serves to local children in need but he explains how hunting is never about “just the hunt” but about the camaraderie, friendship and memories made through the pursuit of the harvest.

programme.title: Winchester Life
programme.desc: In this episode of Winchester Life, Winchester athletes Kim Rhode and Desiree Edmonds share what it takes to compete at the highest level of clay target shooting. From the pressure of national competition to the routines that build confidence, they reveal how preparation, mental focus, and years of dedication lead to success. The transcript emphasizes that managing pressure is a learned skill, supported by consistent routines and trust in dependable equipment like Winchester AA shotshells. - As the two champions train, mentor the next generation, and reflect on the journeys that shaped their careers, the episode celebrates more than trophies. With Kim's Olympic legacy and Desi's Hall of Fame induction, the passion, perseverance, and commitment to excellence that continue to inspire shooters across the country.

programme.title: Winchester Life
programme.desc: In this episode of Winchester Life, Winchester team members and employees meet up at the Keefer Brothers property in Missouri for a multi day deer camp. Along for the ride are outdoor editors Scott Ergas and Dave Hurteau. Chris and Casey are on the search for some large bucks, as well as showing the people at the camp a great time and what deer season is all about.

programme.title: Blair Wiggins Outdoor
programme.desc: Capt. Mike Avinon takes Blair off Naples for a variety of fish.

programme.title: Blair Wiggins Outdoor
programme.desc: Capt. Blair tries for an upgrade off the coast of Naples.

programme.title: The WoodHaven Way
programme.desc: For Mike Pentecost and his son Jacob, Illinois deer camp has become a tradition they look forward to every single year. It’s a place filled with memories, time spent together, and a shared love for chasing whitetails.But this trip carries a little more meaning. At 17 years old, Jacob is heading into his final year of being eligible for Illinois’ special youth season and he and Mike are hoping to make one last trip to deer camp count.

programme.title: Wildbound by Forloh
programme.desc: In part 1 of the British episodes, Andy starts his road trip around the United Kingdom in the Cotswolds where he sets out to hunt and taste the beautiful venison that Michelin star chef, Mark Robinson has to offer. He then proceeds to travel to the border of Scotland where he samples some of the finest and most historic bird shooting practices found throughout the British Isles.
These hunters know the key to taking giant whitetails consistently is all about being in the right place at the right time. Brady Snyder hunts down a giant 200″ buck in Iowa from 2023.

programme.title: HuntStand Presents
programme.desc: For decades, Paul Butski has set the standard in turkey calling. His name is etched into the NWTF Grand National Calling Championships Hall of Fame, and his influence stretches far beyond the stage. He didn’t just win competitions, he shaped the way we talk to turkeys – and more importantly, the way we hunt them.
If you hunt big whitetails this is a must see! Follow Adam Hays and Lee Lakosky as they hunt for multiple giants and learn some tactics for harvesting monster whitetails!

programme.title: Princess Play Time
programme.desc: The proud Princess likes to do things her own way, but her antics are always joined by her restless brother, Prince, who tends to turn everything topsy-turvy. Any playtime in their room transforms into a fantastic journey through unusual worlds: the children arrange a picnic on the Moon, conduct a detective investigation in a toy city, or search for pirate treasures on islands! Although initially, the Princess and Prince seem to clash and compete, by the end, they always find joy in each other's company and that of their cherished dog, Bona.

But even masters need to stop and refuel. When meals or snack time interrupt Ollie’s play, he finds himself confronted with the real challenge of childhood; trying new food. To escape his predicament, Ollie uses his magic spoon to transport himself, along with his sister Poppy, and her stuffy Nummy, to a food planet filled with adventure and the very food Ollie stuck his spoon into.

programme.title: Good Morning Joy
programme.desc: Founder, Glenn Marsden, of Imperfectly Perfect Campaign, and Jeremy Jackson, former Baywatch star share their personal journeys with body dysmorphia and how it led to a worldwide campaign. A young man faces his fears and a tale of kindness at 30,000 ft.

programme.title: Good Morning Joy
programme.desc: Laura Di Franco, CEO of Brave Healer Productions, discusses brave healing and the power of sharing our stories. And, meet Oyen the ginger cat and adorable kids from India, along with Daaji redefining meditation for a joyful heart.

programme.title: Good Morning Joy
programme.desc: Join The Kitchen Psychic, Hannah McKitrick, as we talk ditching diets, embracing food freedom, and finding lightness in mind and body, alongside Susan Noles from The Golden Bachelor for some fun, and meditation leader Daaji discussing compassion.

programme.title: Good Morning Joy
programme.desc: Raelene S. Weaver, author and TEDx speaker who's breaking barriers by normalizing boys' emotions. Witness a touching moment as a man in Italy feels a human touch after 30 years, and Daaji joins for another inspiring segment on our Soul Hugs series.

programme.title: The Emerging Science of Longevity
programme.desc: The body has inherent systems to slow and even reverse aging. When you activate these systems you increase stem cell production, reduce inflammation, increase antioxidant enzymes, build muscle, lose fat, and increase cognitive capacity.

programme.title: The Emerging Science of Longevity
programme.desc: Now that we understand the root causes of aging, how do we actually address the hallmarks of aging? What are the levers we have to optimize our health and longevity? Because medicine has it all wrong. We don't need to treat disease. When we focus on fostering optimal health, disease goes away as a side effect.

programme.title: The Emerging Science of Longevity
programme.desc: There are basic fundamental ways we can optimize our health, starting with topics we’ve already discussed, like eating well and exercising appropriately. But, just as important for health and longevity is the need to rest, relax, and connect with each other. Community is essential, and being of service to one another can help you heal.

programme.title: The Emerging Science of Longevity
programme.desc: Too much stress will take you down, but the right amount of stress at the right time can activate your body's repair and healing mechanisms. What natural elements stress our system in such a way that it then activates the body to heal?

programme.title: Help for the Hurting Heart with David Kessler
programme.desc: Grief is the death of something—someone, a relationship, a job, or a dream. There’s no timeline, and you cannot heal what you do not feel. Guided by David Kessler, this course helps you navigate your river of grief, honor your unique process, and find a path toward healing.

programme.title: Help for the Hurting Heart with David Kessler
programme.desc: Grief is about the heart, but the mind shapes the story we tell. While you can’t change the facts of loss, you can change the narrative, honor old wounds, and choose words that guide you toward growth, meaning, and deeper connection to joy and healing.

programme.title: Help for the Hurting Heart with David Kessler
programme.desc: Loss can make you feel powerless, but grief is your work and your power. David Kessler guides you to grieve fully on your terms, honor your unique process, and reclaim agency over your healing, showing that you can live fully while holding your pain with strength.

programme.title: Help for the Hurting Heart with David Kessler
programme.desc: Your survival mind is wired to protect you from pain, but after loss it can spiral into worry and worst-case thinking. Learn the science of grief, how repetitive thoughts form deep mental pathways, and how to rewire your mind to heal and grow.

programme.title: Compassionate Resilience with Sharon Salzberg
programme.desc: Day 1 introduces the practice of centering through the breath. When the mind drifts to regret or worry, we gently return—again and again. This meditation teaches concentration, presence, and compassion, reminding us that healing isn’t in never wandering, but in beginning again.

programme.title: Compassionate Resilience with Sharon Salzberg
programme.desc: Day 2 invites us to examine the stories we tell about our worth, limits, and lives. By recognizing conditioned habits and outdated coping tools, we reconnect with our power of choice. This lesson reminds us that change is always possible—and that we can meet life with renewed care and curiosity.

programme.title: Compassionate Resilience with Sharon Salzberg
programme.desc: Day 3 focuses on meeting anger and fear with compassion rather than resistance. By paying gentle attention to difficult emotions, we learn they are not bad—only painful when they define us. Using the breath as an anchor, we develop a kinder, wiser relationship to our inner experience.

programme.title: Compassionate Resilience with Sharon Salzberg
programme.desc: Day 4 explores opening to joy by intentionally taking in the good. We examine habits of threat, perfectionism, and resistance, and practice savoring what’s nourishing and life-giving. Through gentle curiosity, this lesson shows how joy can restore resilience and help us meet life with more ease.

programme.title: Phosfate
programme.desc: Cancer survivor and filmmaker Erik E. Crown joins local water activists to investigate accelerated cancer rates and other illnesses in central Florida communities, tracing the source to phosphate mining and the pollution of the state's waterways by a multinational corporation.

programme.title: Artist Friendly
programme.desc: Australian singer, songwriter, and drummer G Flip joins Joel Madden to talk about their rise from session musician to chart-topping solo artist. They discuss growing up in Melbourne, the success of their #1 ARIA album, life in Los Angeles, and lessons learned from years of touring. The conversation also dives into creativity, manifestation, and how G Flip found confidence in their artistry, identity, and marriage.

programme.title: ODESZA: The Last Goodbye Finale Live from The Gorge
programme.desc: Filmed during the sold-out final night of ODESZA’s The Last Goodbye Tour at the legendary Gorge Amphitheatre in Washington, this breathtaking performance blends cinematic visuals, live percussion, and emotional electronic soundscapes. The finale includes two encore songs from the July 5 performance, creating an unforgettable experience from one of electronic music’s most visionary acts.

programme.title: Artist Friendly
programme.desc: Joel talks to British singer-songwriter Maisie Peters about her album Forescence and being a non-identical twin.

programme.title: Future Islands: Live From Cat's Cradle
programme.desc: Future Islands stream live from Cat’s Cradle, celebrating 20 years from a room filled with memories.

programme.title: 10 Years of Noise and Confusion: Oasis Live at Barrowlands
programme.desc: Filmed live at Glasgow’s Barrowlands, Oasis performs Supersonic, Roll With It, and more in a “back to the roots” anniversary show capturing their raw live energy.

programme.title: Rock Concert Cuts
programme.desc: Concert Cuts is an nonstop live rock, featuring electrifying performances from concerts around the world. From iconic anthems to deep cuts, every episode delivers a fresh mix of artists and songs that are coming to you live, loud, and on stage.

programme.title: Salad Days: A Decade Of Punk In Washington, DC (1980-1990)
programme.desc: Acclaimed documentary on punk rock's rise in DC. Bands like Bad Brains booked their own shows. Predated the 90s alternative explosion.

programme.title: Lost Evenings VI: Night 1 – Acoustic Duo with Matt Nasir
programme.desc: The opening night of Lost Evenings VI in Anaheim features an intimate acoustic set from Frank Turner and Matt Nasir. The performance blends heartfelt storytelling with stripped-down versions of fan favorites, including “Be More Kind,” “The Way I Tend to Be,” and a moving duet with KT Tunstall. Turner connects deeply with the audience while revisiting early songs and debuting new arrangements in this special evening of community, humor, and reflection.

programme.title: Artist Friendly
programme.desc: Drummer and producer Cody Hanson of Hinder joins Joel Madden to reflect on two decades of the band’s journey—from college shows in Oklahoma to multi-platinum success with “Lips of an Angel.” They discuss songwriting, evolving as musicians, and the making of their new single “Bring Me Back to Life.”

programme.title: Lamb of God: Killadelphia
programme.desc: Lamb of God's Killadelphia showcases the thrash-metal band at The Trocadero in 2005, featuring a recorded set, candid footage, and an all-access portrait.

programme.title: Artist Friendly
programme.desc: On this week’s episode of Artist Friendly, we’re bringing back Joel Madden’s conversation with Ziggy Marley. Joel and Ziggy go deep on the making of his album Brightside, the song he wrote as a love letter to his father Bob, and what it means to find your purpose without trying to be someone else. One of the most grounded, soulful conversations to date.

programme.title: The Chicks: Top of the World Tour Live
programme.desc: The Chicks, Grammy Award winners, launched their 2003 tour with Top Of The World Tour Live. Enjoy hits like 'Goodbye Earl,' 'A Home,' 'Landslide,' and more.

programme.title: Bowling For Soup: Live and Very Attractive
programme.desc: Bowling for Soup performs live on a U.K. tour, delivering hits like 1985 and Girl All The Bad Guys Want with high-energy pop-punk style.

programme.title: Porno for Pyros: Horns, Thorns En Halos Farewell Tour Live from Los Angeles
programme.desc: Porno for Pyros take the stage one final time for their Horns, Thorns En Halos Farewell Tour, performing live from The Belasco Theater in Los Angeles. Frontman Perry Farrell, guitarist Peter DiStefano, drummer Stephen Perkins, and bassist Martyn LeNoble deliver an electrifying and emotional performance that spans their entire career — from hits like Pets and Tahitian Moon to deep cuts and spoken interludes that showcase their surreal, art-rock energy. Captured exclusively on Veeps, this farewell show celebrates three decades of psychedelic alternative rock and the enduring chemistry that defined the band’s sound.

programme.title: Tomorrow: Scarlet Rae
programme.desc: Scarlet Rae headlines Episode 3 of TOMORROW!, featuring artists and creatives in a visually driven showcase directed by Rebekah Sherman-Myntti.

programme.title: Metal From the Dirt: Rez Metal on the Navajo Nation
programme.desc: Navajo (Diné) musicians and scene builders trace the rise of Rez Metal, from generator-powered desert shows to Hogan rehearsals, blending heavy music with culture, pride, and survival.

programme.title: Artist Friendly
programme.desc: On this week’s episode of Artist Friendly, we’re bringing back Joel Madden’s conversation with Ziggy Marley. Joel and Ziggy go deep on the making of his album Brightside, the song he wrote as a love letter to his father Bob, and what it means to find your purpose without trying to be someone else. One of the most grounded, soulful conversations to date.

programme.title: Maestro
programme.desc: Maestro follows Grammy award-winning conductor Paavo Järvi and brilliant musicians performing in sold-out halls worldwide.
